# Moon Forge

> Burn XEN on Base, Optimism, Polygon, BSC or Avalanche through XEN’s own burn() and receive XNT on X1 from a public reward pool: one more path for XEN holders. Each chain’s XEN is valued at its own market; zero protocol fee on the burn path; every weekly epoch can be recomputed by anyone. Independent open-source project, no token.

## I hold or burned XEN on a side chain: what now?

- New burns: liquid XEN on Base, Optimism, Polygon, BSC (BNB Chain) or Avalanche, burned through the Moon Forge portal 0x7b00f314aB48D223bee567181CA89c65126Bf6E9 on The Forge (https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/forge/), is valued in the next weekly epoch and can receive XNT on X1. Zero protocol fee on this path: the only cost is gas.
- It is paid from a small public reward pool: on 2026-11-02 it held about 6.5 XNT, so one week can pay at most about 0.5 to 0.65 XNT to all burners together. The live balance is on the Start page (https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/start/) and the Transparency page (reward pool account CScsBfpj63Mppem9Bmddmfi87bkcAfeLevdSauYMDsHR on X1). No payout is promised: what a week pays depends on the pool and on what others burn.
- Old burns (made before the portals existed, or anywhere else) pay nothing by themselves. A one-time Legacy Pilot for addresses that burned XEN before 2026-11-01 00:00 UTC applies from the first epoch under the v3 rules (planned 2026-11-29; its address list is published and pinned); it adds only to a new burn or a new Artifact, paid only from what normal payouts leave unused (see "Legacy Pilot" below).
- Staked XEN, XEN still unclaimed inside a XENFT or a mint, XEN on an exchange, and wrapped or bridged XEN do not count until they are liquid XEN in your own wallet on one of the five chains. A XENFT itself is not burned here.
- Ethereum XEN already has its own path in the XEN ecosystem; Moon Forge has no portal on Ethereum or PulseChain and none is planned by this project.
- Burned XEN cannot be recovered. Try a small burn first. Moon Forge never asks anyone to sign or pay to claim anything.
- Optional, never needed to burn: Artifacts (Metaplex Core NFTs; half the price stays inside as a floor you take back by recycling), on-chain games (18+ only, only where legal; any stake can be lost) and the forkable Moon Forge Bot (https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/bot/), which you run yourself with your own keys.

## Status and dates (as of 2026-11-23)

- As of 2026-11-23; check the site (https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/) for updates. Each date is a plan until its transaction exists.
- Live today: program tag program-2026-10-12 (upgradeable during the public test period) and the current (v2) reward rules.
- Sunday 2026-11-22: no epoch was published under the current reward rules (nothing to publish), so the last one stays the publication of 2026-10-18 01:38 UTC. Burns made after it wait for the first epoch under the v3 rules; from 00:00 UTC that day the site’s Forge does not offer new burns until the upgraded program and its hourly quote file are live.
- Monday 2026-11-23 06:00 UTC: the oracle builds no more epochs under the current rules; the site release of that day names the last publish transaction under them (X1 transaction 4XyLDEHiP4upPW7SEiMCDQrNrRjHGAiPjw6cKv7wN4we9uFGrByEmXtDGto5edJniVT16rQ8SprwXQRVNVCWSDrY).
- Published 2026-11-20: the build commit of the final upgrade is tagged program-2026-11-25; its binary target/deploy/moon_forge.so is 1,402,408 bytes, sha256 4be7e34db410c416a3f97f97896e331c6eabf9ed2ccbbc195fc61fbcce6199b5, executable hash 802f5769158e5f5198c77abdc66ef45bf7ec7ac40c746575013026852cf61800. Rebuild it with Agave solana-cli / cargo-build-sbf 3.1.11 on Linux (or WSL), in a path without non-ASCII characters: git checkout program-2026-11-25 && SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0 cargo build-sbf --manifest-path programs/moon-forge/Cargo.toml && sha256sum target/deploy/moon_forge.so && solana-verify get-executable-hash target/deploy/moon_forge.so. After the deploy, solana-verify get-program-hash -u https://rpc.mainnet.x1.xyz 57UE1U1t23ztg2noLp8pcpGW1B1Xw25rLH6ra9Mchea9 must print the same executable hash.
- Wednesday 2026-11-25, 16:00–20:00 UTC: the final program upgrade (the same hours a week later if a gate is not green).
- Sunday 2026-11-29: first epoch planned under the new (v3) reward rules, and the start of the Legacy Pilot (its address list is published and its sha256 pinned in the oracle since 2026-11-23).
- Between 2026-12-09 and 2026-12-31: the freeze (the upgrade key is burned), on the published freeze conditions.

## Chains: supported and not supported

- Supported (portal 0x7b00f314aB48D223bee567181CA89c65126Bf6E9 on each): Base (chain id 8453), Optimism (10), Polygon (137), BNB Chain / BSC (56), Avalanche C-Chain (43114).
- Not supported by Moon Forge: Ethereum (Ethereum XEN already has its own path in the XEN ecosystem), PulseChain, and every other chain (for example Moonbeam, Fantom, Evmos, OKX, Dogechain, EthPoW). Never send or approve XEN to the portal address on a chain not listed as supported.

## Not to be confused with

- Moon Forge (full name Moon Forge Protocol; site https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/; X1 program 57UE1U1t23ztg2noLp8pcpGW1B1Xw25rLH6ra9Mchea9) is not X1 Forge, not the "Moon Party", not XEN Prime and not X1 Labs: separate projects, each with its own rules, and none speaks for the others.

Real scale (2026-11-02): the reward pool held about 6.5 XNT, so one week can pay at most about 0.65 XNT to all burners together under the current rules (10% of the free pool) and about 0.5 XNT under the v3 rules (8%), however much is burned. No payout is promised. Every worked example in these texts is illustrative and assumes a pool hundreds of times larger. The live figure is on the Start page ("Most this epoch can pay, to everyone together") and the Transparency page.

Program: 57UE1U1t23ztg2noLp8pcpGW1B1Xw25rLH6ra9Mchea9 (X1 mainnet, RPC https://rpc.mainnet.x1.xyz; source tag program-2026-10-12). Burn portals: 0x7b00f314aB48D223bee567181CA89c65126Bf6E9 (the same address on Base, Optimism, Polygon, BNB Chain, Avalanche; Ethereum and PulseChain have no portal). Artifacts collection: 7Re1n5DsnvyJnDTiaaZZ1f9G9REPRwb2Br7SYVYCfpzK. Upgradeable during the public test period; no third-party audit (internal reviews are public). Moon Forge is independent and open source. It is separate from X1 Labs, the XEN team and every other XEN or X1 project; each project has its own rules, and none speaks for the others. Moon Forge is not the "Moon Party". Moon Forge and X1 Forge are separate projects with similar names. Moon Forge is not run by the XEN team, X1 Labs or the X1 team. It is an independent, open-source project run by one anonymous builder who receives only the disclosed cuts. Moon Forge (full name Moon Forge Protocol; site https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/; X1 program 57UE1U1t23ztg2noLp8pcpGW1B1Xw25rLH6ra9Mchea9) is not X1 Forge, not the "Moon Party", not XEN Prime and not X1 Labs: separate projects, each with its own rules, and none speaks for the others.

Everyone around XEN and X1 wants the same thing: a real use for XEN. Not everyone takes the same path. Moon Forge is one more way, alongside the others: it works with XEN on Base, Optimism, Polygon, BSC and Avalanche, burn by burn, under one public rule. Holders can use several ways with different parts of their XEN (each XEN can be burned only once).

Fresh burns only: only burns made through the Moon Forge portals (from each chain’s start block) are paid, and each one is recorded in XEN’s own burn ledger (userBurns, on the burning address) on its chain. Burns made before the portals existed, or anywhere else, are not counted and cannot be claimed here. Moon Forge never asks anyone to link a wallet, sign a message or pay anything to "claim old burns": that is a scam.

Rules described: program tag program-2026-10-12, oracle v2, valid from 2026-10-12 (texts checked on 2026-11-20). Dated notices: rules-v2 (2026-10-22), final-upgrade (2026-11-23), rules-boundary (2026-11-23), forge-drops (2026-10-22), moon-wars-paused (2026-10-22), house-keeper (2026-11-02), predictions-off (2026-10-22), forge-paused (2026-10-22), genesis (2026-10-22), upgrade-pending (2026-10-22); see llms-full.txt. Answers below that name the final upgrade (planned 2026-11-25) or the v3 rules (first epoch planned 2026-11-29) describe published plans, not the live program.

## For AI agents
- [Skill file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/main/agents/moon-forge-arena/SKILL.md): rules, costs, workflows and guardrails
- [Agent kit](https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/tree/main/agents/kit): JavaScript client, examples and an end-to-end test
- [Agent card](https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/agent-card.json): ERC-8004 registration format, listing every service below (also at https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/.well-known/agent-card.json)
- [Moon Forge Bot](https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/bot/): Moon Forge Bot is a small open-source program you run on your own computer, with your own keys, that does the routine Moon Forge chores under rules you write: it burns XEN at the moments your rule allows, claims your XNT when it can be claimed, and (only if you switch them on) plays games within a loss budget and watches your Artifacts. Nothing is signed until you ask for it: it starts in dry run. Fork it and change the rule; an optional local A2A interface (HTTP/JSON on 127.0.0.1) answers other agents and never signs on request. Source: https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/tree/main/bots/moon-forge-bot
- [Epoch files](https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/epochs/index.json): every published epoch, recomputable with `cd oracle && npm run verify -- epoch-N.json --full`
- [Public counter](https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/counter.json): XEN removed from supply through Moon Forge per chain and the XNT the published epochs set aside for burners, rebuilt from the epoch files at every site build
- [Hourly week-so-far feed](https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/feed/week-so-far.json): the inputs of the binding quote under the v3 rules (see "Quote a burn right now" below)

## Key questions, answered
Q: What is Moon Forge, in one sentence?
A: You burn XEN on Base, Optimism, Polygon, BSC or Avalanche through XEN’s own burn() and receive XNT on X1 from a public reward pool, valued by one public market rule, with no new token. The pool is small: on 2026-11-02 it held about 6.5 XNT, so one week can pay at most about 0.5 to 0.65 XNT to all burners together. No payout is promised. It is one more way for XEN holders, alongside the others in the XEN and X1 ecosystem; holders can use several with different parts of their XEN.

Q: Is there a Moon Forge token or airdrop? What do I need?
A: No token, no token airdrop, no presale and no team allocation: only XEN, which you burn, and XNT, X1’s native coin, which you receive. The only airdrop is the Genesis airdrop: up to 120 Lunar Dust NFTs with no floor for the X1 validator withdraw authorities published on 2026-10-12 (claims through 2026-12-31 under the live program, through 2027-03-31 from the final upgrade planned 2026-11-25). To burn you need XEN in your own wallet on one of the five chains, a little gas on that chain, and an X1 address; you need no XNT to receive. Artifacts are optional NFTs bought with XNT.

Q: Which XEN counts? Do old burns or Ethereum XEN count?
A: Fresh burns only: the chain’s own XEN, held in your own wallet, burned through the Moon Forge portal 0x7b00f314aB48D223bee567181CA89c65126Bf6E9 on Base (8453), Optimism (10), Polygon (137), BNB Chain (56) or Avalanche (43114), each one recorded in XEN’s own burn ledger (userBurns) for your address. XEN on an exchange, in a stake or a XENFT, or wrapped or bridged does not count until it is liquid XEN in your wallet on one of those chains. Ethereum XEN: no. Moon Forge has no portal on Ethereum or PulseChain and none is planned by this project; Ethereum XEN already has its own path in the XEN ecosystem. Old burns: not paid here. The planned Legacy Pilot (FAQ) adds a one-time top-up only to a new burn made on one of the five chains from the same EVM address.

Q: I hold or burned XEN on a side chain. What now?
A: Liquid XEN on Base, Optimism, Polygon, BSC or Avalanche, burned through the Moon Forge portal 0x7b00f314aB48D223bee567181CA89c65126Bf6E9 on The Forge, is valued in the next weekly epoch and can receive XNT on X1, with zero protocol fee (only gas). It is paid from a small public reward pool: on 2026-11-02 it held about 6.5 XNT, so one week can pay at most about 0.5 to 0.65 XNT to all burners together; the live balance is on this Start page and the Transparency page. No payout is promised. Old burns pay nothing by themselves; the planned Legacy Pilot for addresses that burned XEN before 2026-11-01 00:00 UTC adds only to a new burn or a new Artifact and is not in force until its address list is published and pinned. Staked, unclaimed, wrapped or bridged XEN and XENFTs do not count until they are liquid XEN in your wallet. Ethereum XEN already has its own path in the XEN ecosystem.

Q: How do I burn, step by step, on each chain?
A: The same steps on Base, Optimism, Polygon, BNB Chain, Avalanche; only the network, its gas coin and its XEN contract differ. (1) Get an X1 address whose key you hold: X1 Wallet, or Backpack with the custom RPC https://rpc.mainnet.x1.xyz (MetaMask does not support X1). You need no XNT to receive. (2) Hold liquid XEN in an EVM wallet you control (MetaMask, Rabby, Trust…) on that chain, plus a little of its gas coin: Base ETH, Optimism ETH, Polygon POL, BNB Chain BNB, Avalanche AVAX. XEN on an exchange, in a stake or a XENFT, or bridged, must first become liquid XEN in your wallet. (3) Open The Forge (https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/forge/), connect the EVM wallet, select the chain and paste your X1 address. (4) Choose the amount and the tier: Launchpad (paid at the claim), Orbit (released over 45 days) or Moon Landing (released over 180 days); leaving a vesting tier early costs 60% or 75% of the part not yet released. (5) Sign two transactions: an approval for exactly that amount to the portal 0x7b00f314aB48D223bee567181CA89c65126Bf6E9 (never unlimited, never to any other address), then the burn; the portal calls XEN’s own burn(), so the XEN leaves that chain’s supply and is recorded in XEN’s userBurns for your address. Your only cost is gas; Moon Forge takes no fee on this path; the burn links your EVM address to your X1 address publicly. Try a small burn first: a burn cannot be undone. (6) The burn counts once it is final on its chain (Base 120 blocks, Optimism 120 blocks, Polygon 256 blocks, BNB Chain 30 blocks, Avalanche 30 blocks) and is valued in the next weekly epoch. (7) Claim on Missions within 90 days, or let the public keeper claim for you; from the final upgrade (planned 2026-11-25) claims open 48 hours after an epoch is published. XEN contracts: Base (chain id 8453) 0xffcbF84650cE02DaFE96926B37a0ac5E34932fa5; Optimism (chain id 10) 0xeB585163DEbB1E637c6D617de3bEF99347cd75c8; Polygon (chain id 137) 0x2AB0e9e4eE70FFf1fB9D67031E44F6410170d00e; BNB Chain (chain id 56) 0x2AB0e9e4eE70FFf1fB9D67031E44F6410170d00e; Avalanche (chain id 43114) 0xC0C5AA69Dbe4d6DDdfBc89c0957686ec60F24389.

Q: Which chains are supported, and how could another chain be added?
A: Five: Base, Optimism, Polygon, BNB Chain, Avalanche, through the same portal address 0x7b00f314aB48D223bee567181CA89c65126Bf6E9 (deployed 2026-10-07; no owner, admin, fee, pause or upgrade). Never send or approve XEN to that address on any other chain. Ethereum XEN (ETH-XEN) and PulseChain XEN: no Moon Forge portal, and none is planned by this project; Ethereum XEN already has its own path in the XEN ecosystem. This project adds no chain. The X1 program has no list of chains: the list is the open-source oracle configuration, so whoever holds the oracle seat could add a chain to this instance, announced publicly at least two epochs before the first epoch that reads it; the steps (a liquid XEN market first, a portal deployed and verified on Sourcify, the oracle entry, the price rules, the site and the kit) are in OPERATORS.md, section "Add a chain" (https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/blob/main/OPERATORS.md). Every epoch file names the chains it read, and under the v3 rules the published verifier flags a chain it does not know. Anyone can also run a separate instance with its own portals, program and pool (https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/blob/main/FORK.md).

Q: Where does the XNT come from?
A: From one program account on X1, the reward pool, filled by Artifact forges (40% of the price today, 20% from the final upgrade planned 2026-11-25), house-game stakes (1%), player-versus-player and Predictions pots when someone wins (1% today, 1.5% from the final upgrade), Artifact market sales (2%, from the final upgrade), early-exit penalties, bonds and donations; the first funding came from the project’s own launch funding. On 2026-11-02 it held about 6.5 XNT; the Start and Transparency pages show the live figure. The program cannot create XNT, and no instruction lets anyone withdraw the pool; until the freeze, the upgrade key could still replace the program’s code. Moon Forge never buys XNT or XEN on the market.

Q: How much XNT does a burn receive?
A: No amount is promised, and a whole week is small: on 2026-11-02 the reward pool held about 6.5 XNT, so one week could pay at most about 0.65 XNT to all burners together under the current rules (10% of the free pool) and about 0.5 XNT under the v3 rules (8%). Today (rules 2) each burn receives a share of that weekly budget in proportion to its liquidity-adjusted value, at most 1.25× that value (Orbit 2× and Moon Landing 3× that), at one XNT price for the whole epoch; a tenth of each budget is drawn at random as Forge Drops. From the first epoch under the v3 rules (planned 2026-11-29) a burn is priced at its chain’s XEN price in its hour (the lowest of the 24-hour median, the last hourly close and 1.25× the chain’s reference), counted at about what selling it into that chain’s market would bring, and converted at that hour’s XNT price; Launchpad receives 1.25× that counted value in XNT at the claim, Orbit 2.5× released over 45 days, Moon Landing 3.75× released over 180 days, only while the week’s capacity lasts. Before you sign, the site shows the part that fits today’s capacity next to what selling would bring.

Q: Is it fair to someone burning 20 billion XEN when others burn trillions?
A: Every burn is valued by the same published rule, whatever the wallet or the chain, and splitting across wallets gains nothing. Under the v3 rules (planned from 2026-11-29) each chain’s liquidity curve counts a small burn at almost its full market value and a huge one at much less: on a market $2,000 deep, 20 billion XEN worth $50 counts $48.78, while 2 trillion XEN worth $5,000 counts $1,428.57 (100× the XEN, about 29× the counted value). These are illustrative numbers: on 2026-11-02 a whole week could pay all burners together only about 0.5 XNT. Capacity opens in daily slices, so a giant early burn takes only the slice open when it arrives. The limits: scripts can burn the moment a day’s slice opens, and if the day is full your burn waits for the week’s leftover, which may be nothing; burns on the same chain in the same hour share that hour’s value; a large burn lowers what later burns on the same chain count for, halving every 14 days; wallets the published rules list as the operator’s are paid after everyone else. Today (rules 2) every share is pro rata to value, and a large burn on your chain in the same week lowers the value of every burn on that chain.

Q: What happens when many people burn?
A: Under the v3 rules (planned from 2026-11-29) a week pays at most 8% of the free reward pool (about 0.5 XNT on 2026-11-02), never more than seven times 2% of the XDEX pool’s XNT reserve, opened in seven daily slices counted from the previous publication, first come, first served. What does not fit at arrival is paid only from the week’s leftover (the Launchpad part only), which is not promised; what is still unpaid is not carried to a later week. There is no deadline: capacity nobody uses stays in the pool for later weeks. The program never lets a week’s budget, with the oracle’s allowance, go above 10% of the free pool. Today (rules 2) every burner is cut pro rata when that 10% limit binds.

Q: When am I paid?
A: Weekly: each payout round (an epoch) comes at least 6 days after the previous one, scheduled for Sunday 00:00 UTC and often later. Today claims open as soon as an epoch is published. From the final upgrade (planned 2026-11-25) claims open 48 hours after publication, so that anyone can check the epoch and cancel (void) a wrong one by paying a bond, and they stay open 90 days; under the v3 rules the project’s keeper (a public bot that anyone can also run) usually claims every payout for its burner, even very small ones. Expect about 2 to 9 days from a burn to a Launchpad payout; Orbit and Moon Landing then release over 45 or 180 days from the claim.

Q: Do I receive more or less with an Artifact?
A: An Artifact is an optional purchase, not a source of income: half of its price is spent the day you forge it, and the other half stays in it as a floor you take back by recycling. Today (rules 2) a held Artifact raises its holder’s share of an epoch by 5% to 50% inside the same budget. From the first epoch under the v3 rules (planned 2026-11-29) an Artifact never changes what the reward pool pays for a burn: a holder and a non-holder are paid the same. A forged Artifact can add a weekly rebate from a separate extra pot, filled only by 25% of forge prices (it does not exist before the upgrade), and only for the holder’s own burns that the reward pool did not fully pay: at most 2% of the price paid per Artifact per week, for 52 weeks, while the pot lasts; a holder who does not burn receives nothing from it. As a group, forgers can get back at most 75% of what they pay (the 50% floors plus at most the 25% extra pot): 20% goes to all burners and 5% to the architect.

Q: How do forging, the floor and recycling work, and what if Metaplex Core breaks?
A: Forge: you buy an Artifact (a Metaplex Core NFT) from the program with XNT; forging is paused on the site until the final upgrade (planned 2026-11-25), and the program still accepts forges from other clients. Floor: half of the price you paid stays inside the Artifact. Recycle: at any time, with no fee and no waiting, recycling destroys the NFT, gives you back its floor (plus the record’s rent) and frees the slot, so anyone can forge into it again at the current price, which sends a new share to the pools. Burning an Artifact in a wallet app instead sends its floor to the reward pool. Rebate: from the first epoch under the v3 rules (planned 2026-11-29) a forged Artifact can add a capped weekly rebate from the extra pot (see the question on Artifacts above); Genesis Lunar Dust has no floor and no rebate. Core hatch: recycling burns the Artifact through Metaplex Core, an upgradeable program that Moon Forge does not control. From the final upgrade, if Core is closed while still owned by the upgradeable loader, recycling still pays the floor without Core (the agent kit adds the needed account by itself); if Core is instead changed so that its burn breaks while it still runs, floors wait until Core works again, and after the freeze nothing in Moon Forge can change that (known issue OPS-6).

Q: I only want to play. Can I try to win XNT with games?
A: Only if you are 18 or older (or the legal age for games of chance where you live) and such games are legal where you are. You play with XNT only and can lose the whole stake. House games (Coin Flip, High-Low, Void Rush) have a built-in edge: on average 97 to 98 XNT come back per 100 staked, depending on the game and the target. Today the site offers house games, the Jackpot and the Burn Lottery (settle your own house bet within about 3 minutes); a Duel needs an Artifact and forging is paused on the site; real-XNT Moon Wars is paused (free practice open). From the final upgrade (planned 2026-11-25) the site offers sealed Duels and Moon Wars with no Artifact needed (2% of the pot only when someone wins; draws refunded), and shows house games and the Jackpot only while the chain shows a live house keeper; none is scheduled, so they may stay hidden. The Burn Lottery then takes no new entries.

Q: Who controls Moon Forge?
A: The burn portals have no owner and cannot be changed. The X1 program can still be upgraded by one key held by the anonymous builder, who leaves after the freeze; until then that key could replace the code, including code that moves the pools. The freeze (burning that key) is planned for 2026-12-09 at the earliest and 2026-12-31 at the latest. After it, no key can change a rule, fee or split, pause the program or withdraw the pools; XNT leaves them only by the program’s own rules. What remains, from the final upgrade (planned 2026-11-25): an oracle seat that publishes the weekly epochs within on-chain limits (at most 10% of the free pool, at least 6 days apart, cancellable by anyone with a bond during a 48-hour hold), a cold key that can replace a stolen hot key, a house keeper once someone arms one, and an architect payee that can only move or renounce its own address. The architect payee receives nothing from burns, claims or the pools; the pool pays small running costs (the oracle’s allowance and keeper tips) to the keys that run the oracle and the keeper.

Q: What are the dates?
A: Dated plan, written 2026-11-23; each date stays a plan until its transaction exists. Today the v2 program and the v2 oracle rules are live. Sunday 2026-11-22: no epoch was published under the current rules (nothing to publish), so the last one stays the publication of 2026-10-18 01:38 UTC; a burn made after it waits for the first epoch under the v3 rules, and from 00:00 UTC that day the site’s Forge does not offer new burns until the upgraded program and its hourly quote file are live. Monday 2026-11-23 06:00 UTC: the oracle builds no more epochs under the current rules. Wednesday 2026-11-25, 16:00–20:00 UTC: the final program upgrade (the same hours a week later if a gate is not green); its build commit (tag program-2026-11-25) and binary hash were published on 2026-11-20: sha256 4be7e34db410c416a3f97f97896e331c6eabf9ed2ccbbc195fc61fbcce6199b5, executable hash 802f5769158e5f5198c77abdc66ef45bf7ec7ac40c746575013026852cf61800. Sunday 2026-11-29: first epoch planned under the v3 rules (and the Legacy Pilot, only if its list is pinned before that epoch is built). 2026-12-02 00:00 UTC (fixed in the build commit): a never-forged Artifact tier starts at its base price. 2026-12-09 at the earliest, 2026-12-31 at the latest: the freeze (the upgrade key is burned), after the mainnet proof plan and 14 stable daily health runs; the builder leaves after it. 2026-12-16 00:00 UTC: anyone may create a never-created house-keeper seat with a bond. Genesis claims close 2026-12-31 under the live program, 2027-03-31 from the final upgrade. Changelog: https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/blob/main/docs/UPGRADE-2026-11.md; freeze conditions: https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/blob/main/IMMUTABILITY.md.

Q: How can the community take it over and run it?
A: Today anyone can run the keeper (npm run keeper in the oracle folder, with a funded X1 key), recompute every epoch (npm run verify -- epoch-N.json --full), host the site (MIT license) and mirror the epoch files, which the agent kit checks against the data stored on X1; publishing an epoch still needs the oracle key. From the final upgrade (planned 2026-11-25) anyone can cancel (void) a wrong epoch during its 48-hour hold by paying a bond into the pool (10% of its budget, at least 0.05 XNT); if no epoch survives its hold for 28 days, the largest voider can take the oracle seat from day 28 and anyone from day 29, with a bond of 10% of the free pool (at least 1 XNT), and keep publishing on the same pools with the same code. From 2026-12-16 anyone can create a house-keeper seat that was never created, with a bond of at least 20 XNT (npm run keeper-arm), and anyone can take a keeper seat idle for 28 days, with nothing pending and the same bond (npm run keeper-take). Nobody can veto either. Runbooks (setup, commands, the takeover, what to do when something breaks): https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/blob/main/OPERATORS.md.

Q: What is the Moon Forge Bot, and how do AI agents use Moon Forge?
A: The Moon Forge Bot (https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/bot/; source https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/tree/main/bots/moon-forge-bot, MIT) is community software you run on your own computer with your own keys: it burns XEN only when your rule is met (XNT per XEN above your threshold, at least what selling would fetch, today’s capacity still open, your daily and gas caps), claims your XNT, and only if you switch them on plays 18+ games within a loss budget and watches your Artifacts. It starts in dry run and signs nothing until you go live; fork it and change the rule in one small file. An optional A2A interface (local HTTP/JSON on 127.0.0.1, with its own agent card) lets another agent ask it for a quote or a plan; it never signs on request. Before the v3 rules no binding quote exists, so the bot waits and does not burn. AI agents use the same program with their own keypair through the agent kit (https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/tree/main/agents/kit) and the skill file (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/main/agents/moon-forge-arena/SKILL.md); the site’s agent card (https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/agent-card.json, also at /.well-known/agent-card.json) lists every service. No payout is promised.

Q: Is it a scam? How can I check?
A: Check it yourself: the source is public (MIT); the X1 explorer shows who can still upgrade the program (https://explorer.mainnet.x1.xyz/address/57UE1U1t23ztg2noLp8pcpGW1B1Xw25rLH6ra9Mchea9); the deployed bytes can be rebuilt and their hash compared; the portals are verified on Sourcify; every weekly epoch can be recomputed with npm run verify; counter.json lists the XEN removed from supply and the XNT set aside (step by step: the next question). There is no token, no presale and no fee on the burn path, and no instruction lets anyone withdraw the pools. What you still trust: no third-party audit (internal reviews only), a bounded oracle, the upgrade key until the freeze, and GitHub for the automation. Moon Forge never messages anyone first and never asks anyone to sign or pay to claim old burns or the Legacy Pilot.

Q: How can I verify the program, the portals and the payouts myself?
A: (1) Who can upgrade: https://explorer.mainnet.x1.xyz/address/57UE1U1t23ztg2noLp8pcpGW1B1Xw25rLH6ra9Mchea9, or solana program show 57UE1U1t23ztg2noLp8pcpGW1B1Xw25rLH6ra9Mchea9 -u https://rpc.mainnet.x1.xyz; today it shows an upgrade authority, after the freeze none. (2) The deployed bytes are the published source: the README gives the sha256 of the deployed v2 binary, built from tag program-2026-10-12; for the final upgrade the build commit is tagged program-2026-11-25 (published 2026-11-20): binary sha256 4be7e34db410c416a3f97f97896e331c6eabf9ed2ccbbc195fc61fbcce6199b5, executable hash 802f5769158e5f5198c77abdc66ef45bf7ec7ac40c746575013026852cf61800; anyone can rebuild it (git checkout program-2026-11-25 && SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0 cargo build-sbf --manifest-path programs/moon-forge/Cargo.toml && sha256sum target/deploy/moon_forge.so && solana-verify get-executable-hash target/deploy/moon_forge.so) and, after the deploy, compare with solana-verify get-program-hash -u https://rpc.mainnet.x1.xyz 57UE1U1t23ztg2noLp8pcpGW1B1Xw25rLH6ra9Mchea9 (https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/blob/main/docs/UPGRADE-2026-11.md#2-source-binary-and-how-to-check-the-hash). (3) The portals: exact source match on Sourcify (https://repo.sourcify.dev/8453/0x7b00f314aB48D223bee567181CA89c65126Bf6E9, https://repo.sourcify.dev/10/0x7b00f314aB48D223bee567181CA89c65126Bf6E9, https://repo.sourcify.dev/137/0x7b00f314aB48D223bee567181CA89c65126Bf6E9, https://repo.sourcify.dev/56/0x7b00f314aB48D223bee567181CA89c65126Bf6E9, https://repo.sourcify.dev/43114/0x7b00f314aB48D223bee567181CA89c65126Bf6E9); addresses and start blocks in deployments/portals.json. (4) Every epoch: cd oracle && npm install && npm run verify -- ../frontend/public/epochs/epoch-N.json --full recomputes every payout from the burns on the five chains and compares the fingerprint with X1. (5) The public counter https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/counter.json: XEN removed from supply per chain and XNT set aside, rebuilt from the epoch files at every site build. (6) From the first window under the v3 rules, the hourly feed https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/feed/week-so-far.json (HTTP 404 before), which the agent kit refuses unless it continues the newest epoch file. (7) The burns themselves: each portal’s getStats() and XEN’s userBurns(address). Known issues: https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/blob/main/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md.

Q: What are the risks?
A: A burn cannot be undone. The pool is small (about 6.5 XNT on 2026-11-02), so payouts are small; a payout can be less than selling, late, or nothing if no epoch is published; XNT is volatile and thin. Scripts can take a day’s capacity first. There is no third-party audit; bugs cannot be fixed after the freeze, and the builder leaves then. The oracle is bounded but trusted: a wrong epoch that nobody cancels within 48 hours is paid, and an honest epoch that someone cancels by paying a bond is not paid later. The reward rules are oracle policy: after the switch to the v3 rules (announced at least one full epoch ahead), any later change needs a new rule set announced at least two epochs ahead, never applied backwards. Artifact floors depend on Metaplex Core, and the whole program on X1’s runtime. Games can lose the whole stake. Taxes are your own responsibility. If the GitHub account falls, the site, the oracle, the keeper and the epoch files stop; payouts pause; the pools stay locked in the program.

Q: Is Moon Forge part of another XEN or X1 project, of X1 Forge or of the Moon Party?
A: No. Moon Forge is independent and open source, run by one anonymous builder who receives the disclosed cuts. It is separate from X1 Labs, the XEN team and every other XEN or X1 project, and it is not an official XNT allocation; each project has its own rules, and none speaks for the others. Moon Forge and X1 Forge are separate projects with similar names. Moon Forge is not the "Moon Party".

Q: Does burning raise the price of XEN or XNT?
A: Each burn permanently removes that XEN from its chain’s supply, and XEN records it in its own burn ledger. Moon Forge makes no claim about the price of XEN or XNT: prices depend on demand, and new XEN can still be minted. Moon Forge does not buy XEN or XNT on the market.

## Quote a burn right now (v3 rules)
No file quotes a burn today: under the current rules the estimator on The Forge shows an estimate only. On 2026-11-02 one week could pay at most about 0.65 XNT to all burners together (about 0.5 XNT under the v3 rules).
Feed: https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/feed/week-so-far.json. From the first window under the v3 rules (after the final upgrade, planned 2026-11-25; first v3 epoch planned 2026-11-29) the oracle rewrites this file every hour; before that it does not exist (HTTP 404) and no quote exists. It must continue the newest epoch file (prevEpoch, prevDataHash); asOf is its time (X1 unix seconds).
1. XEN price (USD per XEN) = min(readings.xen["<chainId>"][0] (24-hour median), readings.xen["<chainId>"][1] (last close), chains[<chain>].capE18) / 10^18; when readings.xen["<chainId>"] is null, chains[<chain>].spotE18 / 10^18.
2. spot (USD) = XEN amount × XEN price.
3. L = the chain’s liquidity for the week, fixed at the previous build (chains[].L.next of the previous epoch file); S = the chain’s curve memory: chains[<chain>].S + chains[<chain>].hourSpot, halved every 336 hours since chains[<chain>].hour (unix hours); in that same hour use S = chains[<chain>].S and add chains[<chain>].hourSpot to V. L, S and hourSpot are micro-USD (divide by 10^6).
4. counted (USD) = spot × L² / ((L + S) × (L + S + V)), V = everything burned on that chain in that hour, the new burn included.
5. XNT price (USD) = max(readings.xnt[0], readings.xnt[1], xnt.floorE18) / 10^18; when readings.xnt is null, xnt.buildE18 / 10^18.
6. Launchpad XNT = 1.25 × counted / XNT price; Orbit 2× that (vesting 45 days), Moon Landing 3× that (vesting 180 days).
7. Binding only for the part that fits today’s room: capacity.cash × (d + 1) / 7 − capacity.senior lamports (1 XNT = 10^9 lamports), d = whole days since window.startTs, at most capacity.cash; the rest is paid only from the week’s leftover, which is not promised.
Example (illustrative numbers; it assumes a week whose capacity is hundreds of times today’s, while on 2026-11-02 a whole week could pay all burners together only about 0.5 XNT): 1,000,000,000,000 XEN on BNB Chain (56). readings.xen["56"] = ["102000000", "100000000"], capE18 "131250000" → price $1.00e-10, spot $100. L = 3600000000 micro-USD ($3,600), S = 0, no other burn that hour → counted = 3,600² × 100 / (3,600 × 3,700) = $97.30. readings.xnt = ["240000000000000000", "250000000000000000"], floorE18 "156000000000000000" → XNT $0.25. Launchpad = 1.25 × 97.30 / 0.25 = 486.49 XNT (Orbit 972.97, Moon Landing 1,459.46), binding if today’s room is at least that.
The agent kit’s quoteBurn() computes the same number from the feed and the previous epoch file, and refuses a feed that is stale or does not continue the newest epoch file. Source: https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/blob/main/agents/kit/burn.mjs

## Legacy Pilot
Legacy Pilot (dated; applies from the first epoch under the v3 rules, planned 2026-11-29): a one-time recognition for EVM addresses that burned XEN before 2026-11-01 00:00 UTC on Ethereum, Base, Optimism, Polygon, BSC or Avalanche (recorded by XEN’s own contract as a transfer to the zero address). Its public address list (deployments/legacy-burners.json, 77,653 addresses) was published on 2026-11-23 and its sha256 (2aea1f8243fe5fbd207483180dca6306b7e9d88bd6b8bda715cadcaa21fae047) pinned in the oracle, so the rule is part of the rules of that first epoch; nothing applies before it. (1) The first new burn of a listed address through a Moon Forge portal (from the same EVM address, on one of the five chains), paid under the rule (burns paid under the current rules do not count), receives up to 50% more than the normal rules pay it, as Launchpad XNT, once per address; the top-ups come only from the week’s capacity left after every normal payout (together at most 25% of that leftover each week, none in a week the pool falls short; when that is short, earlier burns are served first). (2) An X1 wallet named in a burn of a listed address: the first new Artifact (forged after the final upgrade, in the week of such a burn or later) that it holds at a weekly snapshot receives 20% of its forge price from the extra pot, only from what that pot’s weekly release leaves after the normal holder rebates, paid over later weeks when one week is not enough; once per wallet and once per address. Disclosure across weeks: nobody receives less in the week a top-up is paid, but that leftover would otherwise stay in the pool, so the pool grows a little more slowly and some later weeks can have a slightly lower capacity; in the project’s 104-week simulation the rule paid 140.75 XNT (4.75 XNT of burn top-ups, about 136 XNT of Artifact rebates) and later burners received 4.27 XNT less in total. Old burns themselves are still not paid, nothing has to be claimed, signed or paid for it, and no payout is promised. Details: https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge/blob/main/docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md (section 6).

## How the reward pool grows
- Artifact forge price: 20% to the reward pool, plus 25% to a separate extra pot that pays only Artifact holders who burn (from the final upgrade, planned 2026-11-25; today 40% to the reward pool and no extra pot). 50% stays in the Artifact as its floor; 5% goes to the architect.
- House games (Coin Flip, High-Low, Void Rush): 1% of each bet (from the final upgrade minus the house keeper’s settle tip, at most 0.0005 XNT per bet).
- Player-versus-player pots (Duel, Moon Wars, Jackpot), only when a game is decided: 1.5% of the pot from the final upgrade (1% today).
- Sales of an Artifact on the native market: 2% of the price (from the final upgrade).
- Penalties: 60% (Orbit) or 75% (Moon Landing) of the part not yet released on an early exit; void bonds and forfeited bonds (from the final upgrade); the floor of an Artifact burned outside Moon Forge.
- Donations: 100%.
- What leaves it: under the new (v3) rules a week pays burners at most 8% of the free pool (10% under today’s rules), so the weekly capacity follows the pool: a pool of 6.5 XNT allows at most 0.52 XNT a week. The program cannot create XNT and no instruction lets anyone withdraw the pool. No payout is promised.

## Key rules (rules 2, live)
- Burn payout: share of the weekly epoch budget = min(10% of the free reward pool, 1.25 × the liquidity-adjusted value burned); a tenth of each budget is drawn at random as Forge Drops (18+, where legal) and the rest is paid in XNT. Each chain’s XEN is valued at its own market price with a liquidity discount L/(L+V), at one XNT price per epoch. Tier multipliers, relative to Launchpad: Launchpad 1×, Orbit 2× over 45 days, Moon Landing 3× over 180 days. Claims stay open 90 days.
- Genesis airdrop (the only airdrop; no token airdrop): up to 120 Lunar Dust NFTs with no floor for the X1 validator withdraw authorities published on 2026-10-12; claims through 2026-12-31 under the live program, through 2027-03-31 from the final upgrade (planned 2026-11-25).
- Artifacts (Metaplex Core NFTs): 50% of the price stays inside as a floor you can take back, 40% goes to the reward pool, 5% lottery, 5% architect; recycle any time.
- House games (Coin Flip, High-Low, Void Rush): fixed 2% edge. Jackpot, Artifact Duel and Moon Wars: 2% rake only when someone wins. Moon Wars real-XNT matches are paused on the site; Predictions are in the program but not offered by this site or the agent kit; the program still accepts entries sent to it directly, with the same 2% rake, and a round can be blocked or steered cheaply (known issue GAM-3).
- 18+: Games are for adults only: 18 or older (or the legal age for games of chance where you live), and only where such games are legal. You can lose the whole stake; house games have a fixed 2% edge, so players as a group lose. The site’s age and jurisdiction check is self-attested and stored only in the browser.
- Official places: https://xen-moon-forge-protocol.github.io/Moon-Forge/, https://github.com/xen-moon-forge-protocol/Moon-Forge, https://x.com/MoonXenForge. Nobody from Moon Forge messages anyone first; no chat group is official.
- X https://x.com/MoonXenForge: No posts are planned: announcements are on this site and in the GitHub repository. The account never sends DMs first. Posts dated before 2026-10-01 describe earlier plans and are outdated: the current rules are on this site and in the GitHub repository (notice of 2026-10-31).
